title: Order of operations, letters and formulae
summary: Work out expressions step by step in the right order. Then let a letter stand for a number and use formulae.
guide: This studio follows Year 6: the order of operations (BIDMAS), simple formulae, and pairs of numbers that satisfy an equation such as a + b = 10.
BIDMAS: Brackets first, then Indices (powers), then Division and Multiplication from left to right, then Addition and Subtraction from left to right.
Tap the operation you want to do first. Each step writes a new line, as in an exercise book. A wrong order is allowed but recorded; use "Undo" to take a step back.
In algebra a letter such as n or a stands for a number. 2n means 2 × n: if n = 5, then 2n is 10, not 25.
A {{term:formula}} such as P = 4a works like a machine: the side of a square (a) goes in and the perimeter (P) comes out.

engine.instruction-order: Tap the operation to do first.

brackets-first.title: Brackets first
brackets-first.prompt: Work out this expression step by step. Predict the answer first. Then each time, tap the operation that comes next.
brackets-first.hint: Brackets first. Then, between adding and multiplying, which comes first?
brackets-first.why: Why shouldn't we work out 3 + 4 first?
brackets-first.model: Because multiplication comes before addition. 4 × 4 means four 4s, and the 3 is added separately: 3 + 16 = 19. Doing 3 + 4 first gives 7 × 4 = 28, which counts the 3 four times.

feedback.not-finished: Not finished yet. Keep going until only one number is left.
feedback.wrong-order: You reached an answer, but the order was wrong. Use "Undo" to go back. Remember: brackets, then × and ÷, then + and −.

powers-and-left-to-right.title: Indices, multiplying, then left to right
powers-and-left-to-right.prompt: This expression has a power, a multiplication, a subtraction and an addition. Predict the answer, then work it out step by step.
powers-and-left-to-right.hint: Index first: 3² means 3 × 3. Then multiply. Finally subtract and add from left to right.
powers-and-left-to-right.success: Right! 3² = 9, 2 × 9 = 18, then from left to right: 20 − 18 = 2 and 2 + 4 = 6.
powers-and-left-to-right.why: Why did you do 20 − 18 first and then add 4, instead of 18 + 4?
powers-and-left-to-right.model: Addition and subtraction have the same rank, so they go from left to right: 20 − 18 = 2, then 2 + 4 = 6. Doing 18 + 4 = 22 first would subtract the 4 instead of adding it: 20 − 22 is a different answer.

feedback.not-finished: Not finished yet. Keep going until only one number is left.
feedback.wrong-order: The order was not right. Use "Undo" to go back. Indices first, then ×, then − and + from left to right.

letter-machine.title: A letter for a number
letter-machine.prompt: This machine works out the expression 2n − 7. Put the input in place of n and write the output.
letter-machine.hint: 2n means 2 × n. For n = 5: first 2 × 5, then take away 7.
letter-machine.model: Because 2n means 2 multiplied by n, not the digit 2 written next to the digit 5. So 2n = 2 × 5 = 10, and 2n − 7 = 10 − 7 = 3. In algebra we leave out the × sign, but it is still a multiplication.

feedback.joined-digits: You wrote the 2 next to n! But 2n means 2 × n. For n = 5, 2n is 10.
feedback.bracket: You took away 7 first and multiplied after. But multiplying comes first: 2 × n, then − 7.
feedback.too-big: One of the outputs is too big. First 2 × n, then take away 7.
feedback.too-small: One of the outputs is too small. First 2 × n, then take away 7.

square-formula.title: The perimeter formula
square-formula.prompt: The perimeter of a square is P = 4a, where a is the length of a side. Write the perimeters. In the last row try any side you like.
square-formula.hint: 4a means 4 × a. A square has 4 equal sides: a + a + a + a.
square-formula.why: Why is the perimeter of a square 4 × a?
square-formula.model: A square has 4 equal sides, and the perimeter is all the sides added: a + a + a + a. Four lots of a is 4 × a, written 4a.

feedback.empty: Write the perimeter of all three squares.
feedback.added: You added 4. But 4a means 4 multiplied by a: four sides, each a long.
feedback.times-three: A square has 4 sides, not 3. The perimeter adds all 4 sides.
feedback.too-big: One perimeter is too big. Work out 4 × a.
feedback.too-small: One perimeter is too small. Work out 4 × a.

make-ten-pairs.title: Pairs that make 10
make-ten-pairs.prompt: a + b = 10. For each a, find the b that makes the equation true. The machine shows b = 10 − a. How many pairs of whole numbers are there from a = 0 to a = 10?
make-ten-pairs.hint: If a = 4, what must you add to 4 to make 10?
make-ten-pairs.success: Well done! 1 + 9, 4 + 6, 6 + 4 and 10 + 0 all make 10. With a from 0 to 10 there are 11 pairs.
make-ten-pairs.why: Why is b smaller when a is bigger?
make-ten-pairs.model: The two numbers must always add up to 10. If a goes up by 1, b has to go down by 1 to keep the total at 10. So every pair is a, 10 − a.

feedback.added: You added 10 to a. But a + b must be 10, so b = 10 − a.
feedback.same: If a = 10 and b = 10, then a + b = 20. What must b be?
feedback.too-big: One b is too big: check that a + b makes exactly 10.
feedback.too-small: One b is too small: check that a + b makes exactly 10.
